messages:
mika: Hey team — prepping a minimal-attack-surface on-prem package for a pilot customer. Two quick areas I want alignment on: RBAC changes needed when we lock down egress and use a proxy for outbound; and KMS integration while using customer-managed HSM behind a private gateway. Also want to surface audit/telemetry retention implications. TL;DR: default-deny egress + locked-down RBAC + external HSM. Thoughts?

samir: +1 to default-deny. Short answer: give the operator controller only the exact verbs it needs (create/watch/update on CRs + get/list for nodes if we use node gating). Avoid cluster-admin in the playbook.

ellie: For egress-proxy pattern, we usually create a service account for the proxy egress gateway and add a narrowly scoped rolebinding for vault/KMS calls. Apps should call KMS via the proxy service — no wide IAM on pods.

jeff: Two gotchas for HSM behind private gateway: a) latency spikes during key ops — plan for fallback caches (encrypted envelope keys). b) attestation: ensure TPM/attestation calls are routed and logged. We stubbed an example flow in the design doc: https://go/internal/onprem/hsm-integration (private).

mika: Good. On RBAC specifics: what policies do we need for emergency ops? We want fast rotation for compromised nodes but not open admin everywhere.

samir: Add an "emergency-rotation" role that grants patch/update to the specific node-pool label selector and a short-lived approval workflow (Slack + 2FA). Automate the request so the role is granted with TTL (1h). Keep a narrow audit scope.

security-bot: [alert] dependency-scan: package lib-kms-connector v2.1.0 has advisory GHSA-xxxx-xxxx. Severity: medium. Recommended: upgrade to v2.1.3 or apply the patch.

mika: Ugh. Can we patch without downtime?

ellie: We can do rolling restarts of the connector daemonset through the egress gateway. Add a readiness probe check that validates KMS handshake before marking ready. Typical rollout: cordon -> drain -> patch -> uncordon.

samir: Also plan for key-material rollback: ensure we keep previous envelope keys for 72h so in-flight decrypts succeed during connector rollouts.

jeff: Example network policy we use for default deny egress (drop-in):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: default-deny-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress: []
```
Add explicit allow policies for the egress-proxy and control-plane agents.

mika: Nice. About audit logs: customer requires 1y retention for KMS audit lines and 90d for general API calls. Any storage sizing rule of thumb?

ellie: For audit throughput, assume 50 req/s peak for a medium pilot (KMS + API). At ~1KB/log -> 4.3GB/day -> ~1.6TB/year. Add 30% buffer. If we ship compressed S3/GCS export, cost is minimal. Ensure logs are signed and immutable for compliance.

ops-oncall: IR checklist snippet for suspected key compromise: 1) Isolate node(s) from egress (apply netpol deny to pods) 2) Revoke ephemeral certs 3) Rotate envelope keys in HSM (or rotate CMK and rewrap) 4) Run consumers with rewrapped keys from new envelope 5) Notify customer + legal if exfil likelihood > low.

mika: Good checklist. Who runs the key rotation? ops or customer?

samir: For private deployments, operator-run rotations are default with customer approval via policy; we support customer-triggered rotations if they want full control. Document both flows in runbook.

jeff: Small operational note: Add a KMS health endpoint that returns last-successful-attestation timestamp. Set an alert if > 30s failure or if attestation fails 3x in 5m. That prevents silent failures during rollout.

security-bot: [info] audit-config: found non-compliant retention policy on cluster 'pilot-1' (audit: 30d). Recommend: update to 90d and enable remote-archive.

mika: I'll update the playbook with these items. Can someone add the emergency-rotation rolebinding snippet to the repo and a netpol template?

ellie: I'll open a PR with rolebinding + netpol template + annotated runbook tonight.

samir: I'll draft the approval workflow and TTL automation (using our ~/.tools/approvals service).

jeff: I'll add the KMS health endpoint and the attestation logging hooks.

mika: Thanks. Last ask — what are minimal isolation guarantees we can promise to customers for pilot? I want a short bullet list for the sales sheet.

samir: Minimal guarantees: 
- Network: default-deny egress and ingress, only allowed paths documented
- KMS: customer-held CMKs, HSM attestation + signed audit logs
- RBAC: least-privilege operator roles + TTL-based emergency elevation
- Logging: remote immutable audit archive (90d+), signed event sequence
- Recovery: envelope key rollback window (72h) and documented rotation playbook

mika: Perfect. I'll craft the outbound note. Marking this thread resolved once PRs land. :thumbsup:

ops-oncall: If anything triggers security-bot alerts during rollout, ping #release-war-room and I'll join.

security-bot: [closed] auto-ticket created: SEC-2025-9123 for upgrade/rollout tracking.
